operations.name: create
operations.handle_obligation: The caller owns the move-only TaskHandle until it is awaited, detached, or dropped.
operations.result_obligation: The promise result is pending and has no readable payload.
guarantees: Async function creation does not execute its body.

operations.name: activate
operations.handle_obligation: start, await, and wait may activate a created handle; a repeated start of an already activated or terminal handle preserves its state and does not create a second execution.
operations.result_obligation: First activation leaves the result pending until terminal completion; repeated activation preserves the existing result state and cannot republish or reclaim it.
guarantees: start queues work and never inlines the task body on the caller stack.
If a structured scope consumes a cold handle, lifecycle and result authority transfer and registry linking commit before activation; ordinary consumed-handle drop cannot intervene.

operations.name: await
operations.handle_obligation: The awaiter is resumed exactly once after the child becomes terminal.
operations.result_obligation: After acquire-observing normal terminal completion, one claimant may privately claim and consume the ready-live result; a canceled result propagates cancellation and does not fabricate a payload.
guarantees: Completion before continuation registration remains linearized.

Normal child-result disposition and parent cancellation share one resolution claim; the awaiting frame uniquely owns a normal-claimed result, while a cancellation that wins first enters the cancel-join-drain path.
A cancellation admitted after normal disposition cannot double-claim the child result, but remains pending for the immediate boundary after mandatory cleanup and may suppress source-visible delivery.
If parent cancellation wins while the child is active, an internal cancel-join-drain barrier reaches child terminal and discharges its result before user continuation or parent finalization.

operations.name: await-outcome
operations.handle_obligation: The awaiter is resumed exactly once after the child becomes terminal.
operations.result_obligation: After acquire-observing normal terminal completion, one claimant may privately claim and consume the ready-live result as Some(T); a canceled result is represented as None without fabricating T.
guarantees: Cancellation capture is explicit at the .await? boundary.

Normal child-result disposition and parent cancellation share one resolution claim; the awaiting frame uniquely owns a normal-claimed result, while a cancellation that wins first enters the cancel-join-drain path.
A cancellation admitted after normal disposition cannot double-claim the child result, but remains pending for the immediate boundary after mandatory cleanup and may suppress source-visible delivery.
If parent cancellation wins while the child is active, an internal cancel-join-drain barrier reaches child terminal and discharges its result before returning None.

operations.name: cancel
operations.handle_obligation: Cancellation requests one observation epoch, wakes or queues suspended work, and may leave a running task running until its next observation boundary.
operations.result_obligation: Unhandled cancellation publishes canceled with no readable payload; explicit current-task cancellation capture may consume that request and later publish an ordinary normal result.
guarantees: Cancellation admitted against an ordinary wait wakes or queues that task and cancels the matching active registrations; a repeated request during AwaitCleanup, ResolutionCleanup, SourceCleanup, or ScopeCleanup coalesces and may help retained work but does not uninstall or win the cleanup-only wait.
Cancellation is inherited by an awaited child through the cancel-join-drain obligation.
The .await? boundary consumes a captured current-task cancellation once and may continue to normal completion.

operations.name: drop
operations.handle_obligation: Dropping a created handle reclaims its frame; dropping an activated handle transfers runtime ownership through detach.
operations.result_obligation: Cold drop destroys frame-owned cede parameters without running the body and publishes canceled before reclaim; when an activated or completed task still has a ConsumerOwned result obligation, drop atomically transfers it to RuntimeOwned(Detached) and participates in the same detach/terminal drain so any normal ready-live result is typed-dropped and published taken before frame reclamation.
guarantees: Owner release is linearized exactly once.
Cold drop discharges every frame-owned no-body cleanup obligation before canceled terminal publication, completion notification, or reclaim.
Activated and completed drop use the two-sided RuntimeOwned(Detached) result drain; neither a late detach nor terminal publication can strand a live payload.

operations.name: detach
operations.handle_obligation: The runtime owns an activated detached task until it reaches a terminal state.
operations.result_obligation: After acquire-observing normal terminal completion, a detached ready-live result is privately claimed once, destroyed through its compiler-installed typed drop entry, and published taken before frame reclamation; a canceled result has no payload.
guarantees: block_on drains runtime-owned detached work before executor shutdown.

result_states.name: pending
result_states.meaning: No normal payload ownership commit or canceled no-payload result has been published.

result_states.name: ready-live
result_states.meaning: A normal result payload has been committed, but no claimant may read or privately claim it until acquire-observing the task's normal terminal state; after that gate it permits exactly one typed transfer or destruction.

result_states.name: taken
result_states.meaning: The unique claimant completed typed transfer or destruction of the normal payload; it cannot be claimed again.

result_states.name: canceled
result_states.meaning: Cancellation completed without publishing a result payload.

proves: created drop does not execute the body
frame-owned cede parameter is reclaimed exactly once
runtime-owned detached work drains before block_on returns
detached frame local is dropped exactly once
canceled await has no fabricated payload
current task cancellation can return a domain outcome
